title: Section 87 — Kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc.

content.overview: BNS s. 87 — Kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc. BNS restatement of IPC 366. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 366. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 87 is the rule on “Kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc”. The section provides that whoever kidnaps or abducts any woman with intent that she may be compelled, or knowing it to be likely that she will be compelled, to marry any person against her will, or in order that she may be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse, or knowing it to be likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and whoever, by means of criminal intimidation as defined in this Sanhita or of abuse of authority or any other method of compulsion, induces any woman to go from any place with intent that she may be, or knowing that it is likely that she will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person shall also be punishable as aforesaid. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 87 exists so that “Kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail

learningObjectives: Master the elements of kidnapping or abducting a woman with intent to compel marriage or force illicit intercourse.
Analyze the second limb: inducing a woman to move by criminal intimidation, abuse of authority, or compulsion for illicit intercourse.
Examine the statutory penalty of imprisonment up to ten years and fine.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 87 criminalizes kidnapping or abducting any woman with intent or knowledge that she will be compelled to marry against her will or forced/seduced to illicit intercourse, as well as inducing a woman to go from any place by criminal intimidation, abuse of authority, or compulsion for illicit intercourse, punishable with imprisonment of either description up to ten years and fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Protects female personal liberty and matrimonial autonomy by penalizing forced marriage and coerced illicit intercourse achieved through kidnapping, abduction, or abuse of authority.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 87 (corresponding to IPC s. 366).
Limb 1: Kidnapping or abducting any woman with intent/knowledge that she will be compelled to marry against her will or forced/seduced to illicit intercourse.

Limb 2: Inducing any woman by criminal intimidation, abuse of authority, or any other method of compulsion to go from any place with intent/knowledge that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse.
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description extending up to ten years, and fine.
essentialIngredients: The accused kidnapped or abducted the woman; OR induced her to go from any place by criminal intimidation, abuse of authority, or compulsion.
The act was accompanied by intent or knowledge that she would be compelled to marry against her will; OR forced or seduced to illicit intercourse.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 87 combines severe protections against forced marriage and sexual exploitation. The first part requires proof of kidnapping (from lawful guardianship if a minor) or abduction (by force or deceit if of any age) accompanied by a specific intent: either that the woman shall be compelled to marry against her will, or forced or seduced to illicit intercourse. The second part expands liability to cases where there is no physical abduction, but the accused uses criminal intimidation, abuse of official/custodial authority, or other compulsive means to induce a woman to leave a place for illicit intercourse. Actual marriage or intercourse is not required; the offence is complete upon the kidnapping/abduction/inducement with the requisite intent.
examples: Teaching example (Abduction for forced marriage): An accused abducts an adult woman from a bus stop at knifepoint, transporting her to a village temple with the declared purpose of forcing her into marriage. The offence under s. 87 is complete the moment she is abducted with that intent.

Teaching example (Abuse of authority): An employer threatens to terminate an employee and ruin her references unless she accompanies him to an outstation guest house for sexual purposes. This constitutes inducing by abuse of authority under the second limb of s. 87.
distinctions: Section 87 vs Simple Kidnapping/Abduction: Simple kidnapping (s. 137) does not require specific matrimonial or sexual exploitation intent; s. 87 imposes an aggravated 10-year penalty based on that specific intent.
Section 87 vs Section 84: Section 84 deals with married women enticed for illicit intercourse; Section 87 applies to any woman and covers abduction/compulsion for marriage or illicit intercourse.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who dragged a woman into a vehicle declaring he would marry her regardless of her consent is liable under s. 87 even though police intercepted the car before any ceremony occurred.
Rule: Section 87 does not require completion of marriage; the offence is consummated upon abduction with intent to compel marriage.
Application: Force was used to move the victim and the intent to compel marriage against her will was explicit.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 87.

keyTakeaways: Aggravated offence of kidnapping or abducting a woman.
Requires intent to compel marriage or force/seduce to illicit intercourse.
Includes inducing a woman to move by abuse of authority or intimidation.
Consummated upon abduction/inducement with intent, regardless of whether marriage occurs.
